extra.message: User input from the 'name' query parameter is interpolated into a Jinja2 template string via f-string on line 38, then evaluated by Template(content).render() on line 41. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax such as {{7*7}} which gets executed server-side, potentially leading to remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape payloads like {{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()}}.

User input from the 'name' query parameter is directly interpolated into an HTML string via f-string without any escaping or sanitization: f"

Hello, {name}!

...". An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript by providing name=, which is reflected directly in the HTML response.

The public_ip value obtained from an external HTTP service response (requests.get on line 31) is interpolated into HTML without sanitization on line 38: f"...{public_ip}...". If the external service is compromised, returns malicious content, or if the PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL is redirected to an attacker-controlled endpoint, the response content is reflected as-is into the HTML, enabling XSS.

requests.get(config.PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL) makes an outbound HTTP request to a URL sourced from an environment variable with no validation of the URL scheme, domain, or port. If an attacker can influence the PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL environment variable (e.g., via CI/CD injection, container orchestration misconfiguration, or the .env_temp template), the server can be directed to make requests to internal services or arbitrary external hosts. The response from this request is also reflected back to users, enabling chained attacks.

SUPER_SECRET_NAME is hardcoded as the string "John Ripper" in source code. This value is committed to version control and visible to anyone with repository access. The FIXME comment indicates it should be loaded from an environment variable but currently is not, making the credential unrevocable without code changes.

SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is hardcoded as the string "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n" in source code. This secret token is committed to version control and visible to anyone with repository access. The FIXME comment indicates it should be loaded from an environment variable but currently is not, making the token unrevocable without code changes.

The Coraza WAF rule engine is set to SecRuleEngine Off, which puts the WAF in detection-only mode. All subsequent security rules (SSTI blocking rule id:1001, SQL injection blocking rule id:1002, XSS blocking rule id:1003, directory traversal blocking rule id:1004) will only log matches but will NOT block any malicious requests. This effectively renders the entire WAF useless as a security control.

The FastAPI application is created with debug=config.DEBUG, which enables debug mode when the DEBUG environment variable is set to True. Debug mode exposes detailed error tracebacks, source code snippets, and internal application state in error responses, which can leak sensitive information to attackers. The .env_temp file in the repository sets DEBUG=True, increasing the risk of this being deployed with debug mode enabled.
